deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous and next pages): n is a prime with n ≡ 1 (mod 3). r is a primitive n-th root of unity, R is a primitive cube root of unity, and g (written ϑ earlier) is a primitive root mod n. The three cubic Gaussian periods are p = Σ_{ind x≡0} r^x, p' = Σ_{ind x≡1} r^x and p'' = Σ_{ind x≡2} r^x. From these Gauss forms the Lagrange resolvent / cubic Gauss sum q = p + Rp' + R²p'' and its conjugate q' = p + R²p' + Rp''. The previous page derived q² = J·q' and q³ = n·J, where J = Σ_{z=2}^{n-1} R^{ind z + ind(z-1)}; in modern terms J is the cubic Jacobi sum J(χ,χ).

(1) Top of page. Gauss writes the Jacobi sum as J = α + βR + γR² = Σ R^{ind(z²−z)}. His 'qq =' is shorthand for the coefficient of q' in q² = Jq'. Here α, β and γ are the numbers of z in {2,…,n−1} for which z(z−1) lies in cubic class 0, 1 and 2 respectively.

(2) Euler's criterion gives (z²−z)^{(n−1)/3} ≡ 1, E or F (mod n), according to the class of z²−z. E and F are the two nontrivial cube roots of unity mod n, corresponding to R and R². Summing over z gives α + βE + γF ≡ Σ_z z^m(z−1)^m with m = (n−1)/3.
- [Implicit step, mine:] the polynomial z^m(z−1)^m has only monomials z^k with m ≤ k ≤ 2m = (2/3)(n−1) < n−1. (Gauss notes the top degree z^{(2/3)(n−1)}.)
- Each power sum Σ_{z mod n} z^k with 0 < k < n−1 is ≡ 0.
- Hence α + βE + γF ≡ 0 (mod n).
[Mine:] the companion sum α + βF + γE ≡ Σ(z²−z)^{2m} has degree 4m > n−1. It therefore picks up the coefficient of z^{n−1}, which is the route to the binomial-coefficient congruence. That sum is not written here.

(3) Lemma on power sums. 1^μ + 2^μ + … + (p−1)^μ ≡ Σ_{k=0}^{p−2} g^{kμ} = (1 − g^{(p−1)μ})/(1 − g^μ) ≡ 0 when (p−1) ∤ μ. When (p−1) | μ, Σ z^{p−1} ≡ p − 1 ≡ −1; Gauss jots 'Σ{z^{p−1}+1}'.

(4) Cyclotomic numbers of order 3. (ij) is the number of x in class i with x+1 in class j.
- Expand (g^i z³ + 1)^{(p−1)/3} by the binomial theorem and sum over all z. Only the k = 0 term (giving p ≡ 0) and the k = (p−1)/3 term survive, so the total is ≡ −g^{i(p−1)/3} = −γ^i. Here γ = g^{(p−1)/3}, i.e. the E of above, renamed.
- Remove z = 0, which contributes 1. The z with g^i z³ = −1 contribute 0; such z occur only for i = 0, because −1 is a cube.
- Each element of class i is hit three times by g^i z³. The result is 3[(i0) + γ(i1) + γ²(i2)] ≡ −1 − γ^i.
- Gauss writes these three congruences as (00)+γ(01)+γγ(02) ≡ −2, (10)+γ(11)+γγ(12) ≡ −1−γ and (20)+γ(21)+γγ(22) ≡ −1−γγ, i.e. without the factor 3.

(5) Symmetry relations among the cyclotomic numbers (for p ≡ 1 mod 6, so −1 is a cube): (00)+1 = (12) = (21) = a, (22) = (10) = (01) = b, (11) = (20) = (02) = c. Substituting into (4) gives Gauss's 'a + γb + γγc = −1'; the correct form is 3(a + γb + γ²c) ≡ 1, i.e. 3a − 1 + 3γb + 3γ²c ≡ 0, as written on the next page.

(6) Multiplication of periods (cf. Disquisitiones §345, §358):
- pp' = (10)p + (11)p' + (12)p''
- pp'' = (20)p + (21)p' + (22)p''
- The third line rewrites pp'' using (5) as (11)p + (12)p' + (10)p''.

(7) Bottom of page: derivation of the symmetries in (5) by substitution. Gauss writes x ≡ γt³, x+1 ≡ γu³ for the (11) case and x = γt³, x+1 = γγu³ for the (12) case; here γ now denotes a non-cubic-residue representative. He then applies the maps x → x/γ, x → 1/x and 1/x + 1 = (x+1)/x = (u/t)³·(…).
- The map x → 1/x gives (ij) = (−i, j−i).
- [Mine:] the map x → −1−x gives (ij) = (ji).
- Together these yield the three classes a, b, c.

The right margin shows the beginning of the table continued on the next page. There Gauss obtains a+b+c = (n−1)/3 and q³ = ½n(M + N√−27) with M = 6a−2−3b−3c, N = b−c, so 4n = M² + 27N². He then gets 9a = M+n+1, 18b = 2n−4−M+9N, 18c = 2n−4−M−9N. Example: n = 97, M = 19, N = 1, a = 13, b = 10, c = 9.
errors: The three congruences (i0)+γ(i1)+γγ(i2) ≡ −1−γ^i omit a factor 3. Each class element is represented three times as g^i z³, so the correct form is 3[(i0)+γ(i1)+γ²(i2)] ≡ −1−γ^i. Check for n=7: (00),(01),(02) = 0,0,1 and γ=2 give 4, while −2 ≡ 5 and 3·4 ≡ 5.
Consequently 'a + γb + γγc = −1' is wrong; it should be 3(a+γb+γ²c) ≡ 1, i.e. 3a−1+3γb+3γ²c ≡ 0. Gauss writes exactly this corrected form on the next page.
The geometric-sum line reads (1−g^μ)/(1−g^μ). The intended numerator is 1−g^{(p−1)μ}, which is ≡ 0; this is an abbreviation or slip.
The third period-product line '(11)p + (12)p'' + (10)p''' is evidently pp'' rewritten via 20=11, 21=12, 22=10. The middle term should multiply p', not p''.
The symbol γ is overloaded: it is first a count (the coefficient of R²), then a cube root of unity mod p, then a non-residue multiplier in x = γt³. This is not an error but is confusing.
'qq = α+βR+γR²' is shorthand: literally q² = (α+βR+γR²)·q', with J = Σ R^{ind(z²−z)}.

results.what: The cubic Jacobi sum J = Σ R^{ind(z²−z)} satisfies q² = Jq', and its coefficients α, β, γ satisfy α+βE+γF ≡ 0 mod n by Euler's criterion and vanishing power sums.
results.modern_name: Jacobi sum J(χ,χ) of a cubic character; congruence for Jacobi sums modulo the prime above p (Stickelberger-type reduction)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disq. Arith. §358, 1801) for the cubic periods; Jacobi (1827/1837) for Jacobi sums

results.what: Σ_{z=1}^{p−1} z^μ ≡ 0 or −1 mod p, according to whether (p−1) ∤ μ or (p−1) | μ.
Computation of the cyclotomic numbers of order 3 modulo p by summing (g^i z³+1)^{(p−1)/3} with the binomial theorem, giving 3[(i0)+γ(i1)+γ²(i2)] ≡ −1−γ^i.
results.modern_name: Evaluation of cyclotomic numbers mod p via Euler's criterion (the method of Gauss's Theoria residuorum biquadraticorum I, applied to order 3)

results.what: Symmetry relations for cubic cyclotomic numbers: (00)+1=(12)=(21), (01)=(10)=(22), (02)=(20)=(11).
results.modern_name: Cyclotomic numbers of order 3 and their symmetries (ij)=(ji)=(−i,j−i)

results.what: Multiplication rules for the cubic periods: pp' = (10)p+(11)p'+(12)p'', etc.
results.modern_name: Multiplication of Gaussian periods via cyclotomic numbers

deep.surprise_reason: This is Gauss's own cubic cyclotomy (Disq. Arith. §358) combined with the mod-p Euler-criterion and binomial-sum technique he published for the biquadratic case in 1828. It leads, on the next page, to 4p = M²+27N² with M ≡ 1 mod 3 pinned down by congruences. The cubic binomial-coefficient congruence is already associated with Gauss and Jacobi. The page is a working draft of known material, with a factor-3 slip that he corrects on the next page.

checkable.sympy: n=7; g=3; cls=lambda x: discrete_log(n,x,g)%3; E=pow(g,(n-1)//3,n); al=sum(1 for z in range(2,n) if cls(z*z-z)==0); be=sum(1 for z in range(2,n) if cls(z*z-z)==1); ga=sum(1 for z in range(2,n) if cls(z*z-z)==2); (al+be*E+ga*E**2)%n==0
checkable.asserts: α+βE+γF ≡ 0 mod n for the Jacobi-sum coefficients (n=7: α=2, β=0, γ=3).

checkable.sympy: all(sum(pow(z,mu,13) for z in range(1,13))%13 == (12 if mu%12==0 else 0) for mu in range(1,40))
checkable.asserts: The power sum Σ z^μ mod p is −1 if (p−1)|μ and 0 otherwise (p=13).

checkable.sympy: p=97; g=5; c=lambda x: discrete_log(p,x,g)%3; C=lambda i,j: sum(1 for x in range(1,p-1) if c(x)==i and c(x+1)==j); G=pow(g,(p-1)//3,p); all((3*(C(i,0)+G*C(i,1)+G**2*C(i,2)) + 1 + G**i) % p == 0 for i in range(3))
checkable.asserts: Corrected congruence 3[(i0)+γ(i1)+γ²(i2)] ≡ −1−γ^i mod p, with the factor 3 that Gauss omits.
Corrected relation 3a−1+3γb+3γ²c ≡ 0 mod p (from the next page).
4n = M²+27N² with M = 6a−2−3b−3c = 19 and N = b−c = 1 for n=97.
For n=7, J = α+βR+γR² = 2+3R² has norm n.

checkable.sympy: p=7; r=exp(2*pi*I/p); R=exp(2*pi*I/3); P=[sum(r**pow(3,3*k+i,p) for k in range(2)) for i in range(3)]; q=P[0]+R*P[1]+R**2*P[2]; qp=P[0]+R**2*P[1]+R*P[2]; abs(N(q**2-(2+3*R**2)*qp))<1e-9
checkable.asserts: q² = J·q' with J = Σ R^{ind(z²−z)} (n=7, primitive root 3).

transcription_corrections: The γ in '(00)+γ(01)+γγ(02)' etc. is a cube root of unity mod p (g^{(p−1)/3}), not the count γ of the first line.
'(1−g^μ)/(1−g^μ)': the intended numerator is 1−g^{(p−1)μ} (or the line is abbreviated).
Third period-product line: probably '= (11)p + (12)p' + (10)p''' (a rewriting of pp''); the manuscript/transcription shows p'' in the middle term.
'(00) [-...-] (gz³+1)' : the struck-out part precedes '(gz³+1)^{(p−1)/3}'; read the expression as (g^i z³+1)^{(p−1)/3}, whose residue 1, E, F corresponds to (00), (01), (02).
The right-margin column is the left edge of the next page (the table a−1, b, c, b, c, a, c, a, b for 00…22), not part of this page's argument.
